note: Slides for the first supporters meeting, in five acts: open, what the data says, what we did about it, over to the room, and what happens next. Every figure is pulled live from the consultation and the letters at render time and none of it is typed into this file. `say` is a note to whoever is presenting and is never shown to the room or to the public.

slides.title: Two hours, and most of it is yours.
slides.say: Ten seconds. Say the questions block is forty five minutes, that it is the point of the night, and that we finish on what we are actually going to do.

slides.title: 199 supporters answered in five days.
slides.body: Nobody was paid and nobody was chased. 181 of them asked for a meeting: 118 in a room, 71 online, 31 who could not come but wanted keeping posted. This is us getting on with it.
slides.say: Short. This is the answer to anyone who thinks the working group appointed itself, so say it once and let it sit.
slides.method: We ran a survey from Monday 17 August to midday on Friday 21 August 2026 - five days - through this app. Anyone could answer, with or without an account, one response per device. Nine questions, seven of them multiple choice and two free text. Nobody was paid, prompted or selected.

slides.say: Read the second number out and stop talking. Ninety six people choosing the lowest score there was is the single hardest fact of the night.

slides.eyebrow: The first thing the data says
slides.title: This is not about the football.
slides.say: The most important slide in the deck and the one most likely to be misrepresented afterwards. Say plainly: nobody in this room is here because results are bad. The team is the thing supporters are proudest of.

slides.title: Five things, and they are not close.
slides.say: Do not read all seven. Name the top three, say that more than eight in ten supporters picked each of them, and move on.

slides.eyebrow: Who supporters feel speaks for them
slides.title: Four in five feel the ownership does not represent them.
slides.say: Be careful and be fair here. This is how supporters feel, which is a fact about supporters, not an accusation about any individual. Say it exactly that way.

slides.title: Three companies, one football club.
slides.checked: Companies House, public record, checked 31 August 2026

rows.name: Kettering Town F.C. Management Ltd
rows.note: The company that runs the club. Its accounts are filed and up to date.

slides.foot: Nothing here is unusual and none of it is an accusation of anything at all; it is purely for fan awareness. We raise it once and leave it. We have asked the question and we are not going to spend tonight on it.
slides.say: Sixty seconds, then move on, and say the last sentence of the slide out loud. This is on the record and we have asked about it. It is not what tonight is for, and a room that spends an hour on company numbers has not built anything.

slides.eyebrow: Who the club says runs the club
slides.title: Twenty nine roles, four of them still to be announced.
slides.body: Straight off the club's own Officials page. Not our list, not a comment on anybody on it, and worth having in front of us because one of the twelve questions asks the club to name the board with the date each person took their role.
slides.say: Do not read the names out. Point at it, say it is the club's own page copied on the day, and move on. The only thing worth saying aloud is the number still marked TBA - and say it as a fact, not as a dig.

slides.eyebrow: What supporters said they would back
slides.title: Only one in nine would rather it was left alone.
slides.say: This is the mandate for the last part of the night. Note that eleven per cent would rather it was settled quietly, and say so: that is a real answer and those people are in the room too.
slides.note: chose “nothing, I would rather it was settled quietly”. That was on the form as a real answer, and hopefully there are a few in this camp in this room too.

slides.title: Twelve questions, in writing.
slides.body: Ten of them came straight out of what supporters wrote in the consultation. Two were added by the working group after the reply to the first letter.
slides.say: Do not read all twelve. Say they are all on the app and pick the two you most want the room thinking about before questions open.

Say they replied, and say they replied on time, before you say anything else about it. The room will have seen it. If the first thing out of your mouth is a criticism you look like you were never going to be satisfied, and you hand them that for free.
slides.unanswered: of the questions are answered and the email has not been acknowledged.
slides.replied: The club replied at 7:45am on Wednesday 3 September, a day inside the date we asked for. It is published in full on the letters page. It does not answer the twelve one by one, and we have said which against each.

slides.eyebrow: What we think supporters should have sight of
slides.title: Six things, and none of them are huge.

points.ask: Explain the volunteer departures, and set out how volunteers are recruited, supported and kept.
points.backs: The largest concern in the consultation - 92% of 199

points.ask: Answer the twelve questions in writing, and publish the answers. Chase if not received.
points.backs: Sent 22 August, with a reply asked for by 4 September

points.ask: Name everyone on the board and any committee, with their role and the date they took it.
points.backs: 71% say the board represents them badly or very badly

points.ask: Meet a recognised supporters’ body regularly, on a set date, on the record.
points.backs: 83% say the ownership does not represent them; 97 asked for a public meeting (hopefully some of you are here)

points.ask: Set out which company holds the ground, the lease and the debts.
points.backs: Three companies on the public record; supporters cannot tell which, and that drives confusion and sometimes division among fans

points.ask: Publish a financial health report that a supporter can read: income, where it comes from, and what it is spent on.
points.backs: Financial sustainability is a huge fan concern, mentioned by 86%. The filed accounts do not show a clear picture

slides.say: Six asks, each already put to the club in writing and each backed by a number. Read the ask, not the evidence line. Agree the wording with the working group before the night.

slides.eyebrow: Before anybody says we are a small club
slides.say: Say the number once, flatly, then the line under it, then stop. This is the bridge into the rest of the night: do not let it sit there as a boast about how big we are, because on its own that is all it is. The point is that the difficult half is already done.
slides.body: This stat is not here to boast. It shows, in theory, an average of about 170 fans going through the gate at every away ground, and nobody organised it. No committee, no membership, nobody asking. It is just what this support does. Which means the hard part - getting people to care and turn up - is already done. The only thing missing is structure.

slides.eyebrow: What we are actually trying to build
slides.title: An association that outlasts any one of us.
slides.blurb: Four jobs. None of them is full time, none needs an accountant, and none of them is currently filled by anybody who put their hand up for it.

points.backs: Runs the meetings, speaks for the room, and keeps things moving along with a bit of diplomacy.
Writes down what was agreed and publishes it, so nothing rests on anyone's memory.

points.ask: Someone for graphics and the digital side
points.backs: All of it so far has been built from the ground up, solo. We want somebody to help turn art into life, and we would love to platform your work too.

points.ask: Someone to talk to the club
points.backs: One named person, so the club has somebody to answer and cannot say it did not know who to ask.

slides.say: Say plainly that none of these four is filled. Do not make it a plea - make it a job description, because people volunteer for jobs and back away from pleas.

slides.eyebrow: How we could do it, and how fast
slides.title: Most of this can be settled tonight.

rows.what: Agree the Association exists, and elect an interim committee or working group from the floor.
rows.why: Interim, so nobody is signing up for life, anybody can change their mind, and nobody has to have read a constitution.

rows.what: Name someone to write to the club as a representative and collator of fan feedback.
rows.why: Fans have not been listened to properly for years, over and over. We want that to change.

rows.what: A short constitution or founding document - two pages, not twenty - published for everyone.
rows.why: It says who can join, how officers are chosen, and how they can be removed. That is most of it.

rows.what: A proper election, open to every member, at a second meeting.
rows.why: Whoever steps up tonight stands again in the open. Nobody inherits anything.

slides.say: This is the slide the night turns on. Take it slowly. The word to lean on is interim: it is the thing that makes standing up feel survivable.

slides.title: This should not be my association. It is yours.
slides.body: I built the app and I am happy being the person who keeps growing it - I genuinely enjoy it. Somebody had to start this and nobody else was doing it, so I did. But a supporters' association that depends on one person, or on a small working group, is not an association. Fan representation is the whole point of it.
slides.say: Your call whether to say this at all. If you do, say it once, without apology, and then be quiet and let the room answer. Do not soften it into a joke - the honesty is the whole reason it works.
slides.aside: Only through a group effort is this going to get off the ground. If the interest is not there it stays a web app, focused on the matchday experience and nothing more. Our club has a lot more potential than that, and our history is something we should be proud of and aim to preserve.

slides.title: Your questions, in the order you backed them.
slides.say: Hand over. Forty five minutes. This is the half of the night that matters and the half that will be remembered.

slides.title: Nothing on this slide happens without a name against it.
slides.say: Work down the list. For each one ask for hands, then ask who will actually help. Anybody can add one from their phone right now and it appears here. Do not leave the room until at least two have a helper.

slides.title: Everything tonight was done by supporters in their own time.
slides.body: Thank you to everyone involved in arranging it, and thank you for coming. The consultation, the letters, the app, this room. If you want to help with any of it - the archive project, away travel, the letters - say so before you leave, put your name against something on the app, or come and speak to one of us.
slides.say: Finish on the ask, then get out of the way and let people talk.
